title: Machine learning guides magnetocaloric Laves-phase synthesis
summary: Three machine-learning models predicted Curie temperatures to select Nd–Pr–Co–Ni and Pr–Ce–Co–Ni Laves-phase compositions, which were synthesized by arc melting and characterized. The Nd–Pr compositions showed magnetic ordering between 20 and 36 K and reported magnetic entropy changes of 6.0–7.2 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 5 T. The authors caution that predictions lack precision and do not show superiority over other light-rare-earth compounds; no working hydrogen liquefier is demonstrated.
ai_technology: Random forest; gradient boosting; neural-network regression

evidence.tested: Primary full text reports synthesis and characterization, magnetic ordering and magnetocaloric measurements for ML-selected compositions.
evidence.unknown: Independent replication and broader application are not established by this bounded review.
evidence.ai_role: Models estimate Curie temperature to guide composition selection; researchers synthesize and measure selected Laves phases.

source_review.scope: Author-institution repository PDF full text and publisher metadata; composition-level previous-work comparison is bounded, not exhaustive.
